inclusion.I1: Empirical English language MRI studies assessing grey matter (GM) volume differences between substance users and controls

exclusion.E3: Studies including participants with reports of mental and/or neurological disorders

inclusion.I2: Empirical English language MRI studies assessing grey matter (GM) volume differences between substance users and controls
inclusion.I3: Whole-brain evidence- The paper must report at least one whole-brain between-group contrast of substance users vs controls comparing GM volume
inclusion.I4: It is acceptable for qualifying voxelwise results to be reported in tables of coordinates, figures, or supplementary materials when the main text clearly indicates those results are available.
inclusion.I5: Reporting of participant age/sex, cue type, MRI field strength, and preprocessing/statistical software is preferred; missing one or more of these details alone should not exclude an otherwise qualifying study.

exclusion.E5: Studies that report only region-of-interest (ROI) analyses with no qualifying whole-brain results.
exclusion.E6: Non-empirical papers (e.g., reviews, meta-analyses, methods-only, simulations) without original human fMRI data.
